standard_prerequisites.name: Connectedness of a map through its homotopy fibres
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is 0-connected exactly when the 0-truncation of each of its homotopy fibres is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the unfolding of the goal at the start of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: The map k is surjective
standard_prerequisites.statement: The map from the set of generators to the base is (-1)-connected, that is, every element of the base is merely a value of it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It lets the proof assume the point of the base is a value of the map, because contractibility is a mere proposition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equality in a homotopy fibre and in a set
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two points of a homotopy fibre are equal as soon as the underlying points and the transported paths agree, and in a set all parallel equalities coincide.
standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives the equality of the chosen point with an arbitrary point, and the second discharges the case of the path constructor automatically.

core_obligations: Unfold the goal: for every point of the base, the 0-truncation of its homotopy fibre of the induced map is contractible (source line 2165).
Reduce to the case where that point is a value of the map k, which is legitimate because contractibility is a mere proposition and k is (-1)-connected (source line 2166).
Take the centre of contraction to be the truncation of the pair formed by the chosen generator and the equality exhibiting it as a value of the induced map (source line 2167).
For an arbitrary element of that truncation, assume it is the truncation of an explicit pair by the set-ness of the type (source lines 2169-2170).

Induct on the point of the total space: in the generator case the equality p yields an equality of generators through the path constructor, hence an equality of the two pairs in the homotopy fibre and so of their truncations (source lines 2172-2174).
Discharge the case where the point varies along the path constructor: the equalities to be compared lie in a set, so it is automatic (source lines 2175-2176).

proof_roadmap.step: Unfold the goal, reduce to a value of k, and choose the centre of contraction.
Arbitrary point: assume an explicit pair and show it equals the centre by induction on the total space.
The path-constructor case is automatic because the type is a set.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 2161-2163: the induced map on the total space of the cover is 0-connected. The proof (source lines 2164-2177) carries the whole argument and is not visible in the statement: it unfolds connectedness through homotopy fibres, uses that contractibility is a mere proposition together with the surjectivity of k to reduce the base point to a value of k, builds the centre of contraction explicitly, then takes an arbitrary element of the truncation, uses the set-ness of the fibre truncation to assume it is given by an explicit point and path, performs an induction on the total space where the generator case is turned by the path constructor into an equality of homotopy-fibre points, and finally discharges the path-constructor case from set-ness alone. The reduction chain and the induction are the substance.
